name: Primary Failure of Tooth Eruption

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Failure of Tooth Eruption

criteria.description: Failure of eruption of one or more permanent teeth despite normal root formation
Absence of mechanical obstruction or ankylosis preventing eruption
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Radiographic evidence showing normal root development with failure of eruption

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of failure of eruption of permanent teeth with normal root development and absence of mechanical obstruction or ankylosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for PTH1R mutations may support diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Non-eruption of permanent teeth despite normal root formation
searchTerms: permanent teeth not coming in despite normal roots
failure of adult teeth to emerge

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure of tooth eruption in absence of mechanical obstruction
searchTerms: failure of teeth to come through gums
no mechanical cause for missing teeth

common.symptomName: Delayed eruption of multiple permanent teeth
searchTerms: late coming in of adult teeth

common.notes: May cause functional and aesthetic issues
searchTerms: crooked teeth due to missing eruption
bad bite caused by trapped teeth
primary teeth coming in on time

common.symptomName: Family history of similar eruption failure
searchTerms: family members with tooth eruption problems
hereditary failure of teeth to emerge
roots of trapped teeth breaking down
infection in teeth stuck under gums
one side of face slightly different
pain when teeth try to come in

imaging: Radiographs showing unerupted permanent teeth with normal root formation
Absence of mechanical obstruction or ankylosis on imaging
genetic: Mutations in PTH1R gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing failure of eruption despite normal dental development

distinguishingFeatures: Radiographic evidence of fusion between tooth and alveolar bone
Usually localized to a single tooth
Presence of physical barriers such as supernumerary teeth or cysts
Normal eruption pattern of unaffected teeth

redFlags: Sudden onset of pain or swelling in area of unerupted teeth
Signs of infection or abscess formation around impacted teeth
references: Frazier-Bowers SA, et al. Primary failure of eruption: a review and case reports. Pediatr Dent. 2007;29(4):345-351.
